title: The Cider Ratio Riddle
story: Parchleaf the Orchard Miser will only release the frozen apple pickers if Mr 6 mixes her winter cider exactly right: sour apples to sweet apples in a ratio of 3 to 5. Mr 6 has a barrel that holds exactly 344 apples, and it must be filled to the brim.
question: How many sweet apples go into the barrel?
hint: The ratio 3:5 makes 8 equal parts. Find the size of one part first.
victory: The cider comes out perfect, Parchleaf takes one sip and melts into happy tears, and the pickers thaw out laughing. Mr 6 gets the first mug.
imagePrompt: A gaunt bark-skinned miser guarding a frost-covered orchard and a giant cider barrel, with a number-six knight sorting sour and sweet apples into measured heaps under pale winter light.
solution: The ratio 3:5 makes 3 + 5 = 8 equal parts of the 344 apples.
The sweet apples are 5 parts: 5 × 43 = 215 apples.
praise: Using the ratio was smart thinking — finding the size of one part (344 ÷ 8 = 43) was the missing bridge.
